request.query: I manage a wholesale business. All figures are GBP and relate to one year. Revenue is £960,000, sales returns are £24,000, opening inventory is £85,000, purchases are £570,000, and closing inventory is £95,000. Salaries are £140,000, rent £42,000, utilities £18,000, depreciation £22,000, and interest £9,000. Calculate net sales, cost of goods sold, gross profit, gross margin, total operating expenses, operating profit and profit before tax. Show formulas and a results table. Explain the difference between inventory, an expense and a cash payment. Do not assume purchases were paid immediately. Finish with two questions management should investigate.

answer.text:
### Calculation
- Net sales = £960,000.00 − £24,000.00 = £936,000.00
- Cost of goods sold = £85,000.00 + £570,000.00 − £95,000.00 = £560,000.00
- Gross profit = £936,000.00 − £560,000.00 = £376,000.00
- Gross margin = £376,000.00 ÷ £936,000.00 × 100 = 40.17%
- Operating expenses = £140,000.00 + £42,000.00 + £18,000.00 + £22,000.00 = £222,000.00
- Operating profit = £376,000.00 − £222,000.00 = £154,000.00
- Finance costs = £9,000.00 = £9,000.00
- Profit before tax = £154,000.00 − £9,000.00 interest = £145,000.00

### Result
| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Net Sales | £936,000.00 |
| Cost Of Goods Sold | £560,000.00 |
| Gross Profit | £376,000.00 |
| Gross Margin | 40.17% |
| Operating Expenses | £222,000.00 |
| Operating Profit | £154,000.00 |
| Finance Costs | £9,000.00 |
| Profit Before Tax | £145,000.00 |

### Notes
- Interest is a finance expense deducted after operating profit; it is not included in operating expenses.
- Inventory is an asset held for sale. Cost of goods sold is the expense recognised as inventory is sold. A cash payment is a separate cash outflow: the purchase figures do not establish when suppliers were paid.
- Management question: do stock counts, purchase records and inventory valuation support the closing balance?
- Management question: what do receivables, supplier payment terms and cash records show about working capital?
